utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Unfortunately, we could not start earlier since the initial appearance started with a considerable delay. Therefore, we are suffering from the same technical problems. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness, Mr. Gray, into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Gray.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could start only a bit later because the previous session -- started also late because of technical problems. May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Now, the Prosecution will resume its cross-examination. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Ierace: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Gray.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hello, how are you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because we both speak the same language, even the same inflections --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not quite. A important distinction. I have been warned by the interpreters to ensure that there is a pause between --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we speak?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I must speak a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could also the witness speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And also into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that you were in Sarajevo between the 10th of April and the 20th of September, 1992. General MacKenzie was there between the 13th of March, I think thereabouts, and the 25th of July, 1992; is that as you remember it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was broken in two different points. I mean he was there, he may well have been there from 23rd of March but he actually withdrew with the rest of the UNPROFOR headquarters on the 15th and 16th of May and then came back again later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was away, I think, at that stage for some three weeks in Belgrade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll come back to that. I think you were there at that period as well, at that stage as well?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was still there in --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could there be a break please between question and answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I again remind you, Mr. Gray, to just have a short break before starting to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from breaks in his tenure in Sarajevo, is it your understanding that he arrived for the first time in mid-March and left towards the end of July for the last time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the understanding that he -- I don't know when he actually arrived there, I have no idea of that. He was there when I arrived there and then he left and then he came back and yes, he did leave in the end of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was your immediate superior Colonel John Wilson?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you understand that he had been in Sarajevo also from mid-March 1992?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he leave around the 24th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He left at I think 1400 hours on the 24th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I notice you've got a document that you've pulled out of your briefcase, can you just tell us what type of document that is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a sitrep which is signed by Brigadier John Wilson, he was promoted, and it was a situation report of what was happening and what had happened to me in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I just have a quick look at that document? When you say it's a sitrep, is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is the -- is the Defence aware of the content of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know. I do not know this document. I think that for courtesy we should also be shown that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Certainly for courtesy but also for trial reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's a four-page document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but I got the impression that you would like to ask a question about the document and then I think it would be proper that the Defence has had an opportunity at least to look at what the document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Well, I'll pass it to the court orderly now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would first give an opportunity also in time to the Defence to just briefly inspect for the document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please wait. I need to see what the document is about. Thank you, in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Questions about a document, I can imagine that Mr. Ierace puts the next question to the witness if it's not about the document. Perhaps he will ask no questions at all about the document then you will have a further opportunity to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President, because I do not know whether what Mr. Ierace has just discovered can be used -- can be useful to him. We need to -- and before I read the document I cannot look at the transcript, listen to what Mr. Ierace is saying and read the document at the same time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was your next question in any way influenced by knowledge of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In that view, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, I want to ask you some questions about the history of the PTT building and --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- The UN mission. And I appreciate that these questions predate, in part, your time in Sarajevo. Was it your understanding that when the UN came to Sarajevo, the reason was to establish a base for the operation of the UN forces in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that stage, and I'm referring to March 1992, there was no mission, no mandate to get involved in the affairs of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only reason that Sarajevo was selected was because it was a safe distance from the conflict in Croatia and there was a major airport; was that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a serious mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll leave that to one side for a moment, whether it was --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: But yes, that is why it happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you can keep in mind to wait for a few seconds before you answer. Now, was it your understanding that when General MacKenzie arrived in mid-March that the first building utilised by those UN forces was the Holiday Inn hotel, that was the very first place that was used?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thereafter, at some stage thereafter, the Bosnian government made available to the UN the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the PTT building was effectively a government technical facility that supported the telephone industry; is that your understanding of what its function was, at least prior to the conflict in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was and it was very technical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it have a five-storey tower connected to a three storey building and a number of subfloors including a bunker and a parking lot?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, did all government buildings or at least most have a bunker as a legacy from the days of the former Yugoslavia in terms of defensive -- Defence requirements?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of the cold war, most buildings, large buildings, apartment buildings in Sarajevo had subbasements and they also had generators there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah. Now, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can remind you to stop to make a break. I know it's difficult, you easily forget about it but for the interpreters, it's a very difficult task.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the last thing on anyone's mind when the PTT building was selected was that its role would be anything like what it became; is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that means that its position in relation to what ultimately became the warring factions, its position in relation to the confrontation lines clearly could not have been a consideration at the time that it was allocated and accepted by the UN -- allocated to and accepted by them?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that there was a workshop in the PTT building and would it be fair to say that when it was first occupied by the UN, there could be no reasonable complaint about that engineering facility being used by the government, by the Presidency at that stage, being pre-conflict?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no one actually using the workshop. I mean when the UN took over the PTT building, the building apart from a few administrative workers had been totally vacated. There were no engineering staff at all in the workshop area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you say apart from a few administrative workers, were they workers involved with the UN or with government business, Bosnian government business?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were a part of the PTT.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in terms of the Rainbow hotel, is it your understanding that that was initially an old people's home about 800 metres west of the PTT building built, but not occupied, that was made available by the Bosnian government authorities to the UN for accommodation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was actually vacated, it was actually occupied. It had staff in it. And it was vacated in order that the UN occupy it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived on the 20th of April, was it already occupied by the UN?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 10th of April, and yes, it was occupied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in particular, was it occupied or allocated for offices with the rank of major and below?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That all changed when Sarajevo went the same way as Croatia, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you need to clarify your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the appropriateness of the PTT building and the Rainbow hotel, cast in the light of the conflict that broke out, the appropriateness of those buildings was a different answer -- different question, I should say.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it definitely changed and you need to also take into account the buildings which were up in -- they were up in around Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to other UN buildings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, where the seen your staff was based but when the conflict started, the whole situation changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And suddenly the UN found itself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, may I ask you also for pauses and breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And suddenly within the space of a few months, the UN found itself with its headquarters a matter of metres, 50 metres, perhaps, from the confrontation lines, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't. We found the UN headquarters was approximately 400 metres from the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown the map that he had yesterday, the Defence map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is 1845. It consists of two parts and I take it -- yes, Madam Registrar. I take it that the westerly part is needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point to the closest part of the confrontation line to the PTT as of the 20th of September, 1992 and could we have the ELMO zoom in on that position as the witness holds the pointer. Perhaps we can zoom in a little closer.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now you have placed the pointer on point nine, that is the student hostel.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It also includes the apartment building that I actually occupied which is here. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You now have the pointer --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. That was the front line, okay? The student building and my apartment building and the buildings that were occupied or were occupied by military observers are here. They're right here. That was the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just pause for a minute. The witness indicates Ante Babicka Street and moves the pointer along that street between point 9 and a distance south of point 3. Now, was there a no man's land from that part of the front line to the Bosnian Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was. There was a no man's land which existed in this area here between where I indicated before and Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the building complex as the school for the blind or the home for the blind?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take your pen and --?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President might I be reminded whether it's black or blue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's blue, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you mark, according to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, may I ask you only to use the pen handed out to you by the usher. I see that we are using different colours for markings made on request of the defendant. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, firstly the most forward front line position of the Presidency forces in the vicinity of the PTT. Would you please indicate with the pen and draw where that line went north of what you have already marked?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult because the line was so irregular, I mean it went something like -- because Papa 7 was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please stop for a moment. Please stop.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me focus your attention back on position number 9. Do you remember where that front line continued from the most northwards, most northerly position that you have so far marked. If you don't, just let us know.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean it went straight, basically north from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please mark the most forward Bosnian Serb positions opposite the front line position you've already drawn for the Presidency forces as of the 20th of September, 1992. And do you say that -- well, firstly, would you describe the area between the two front lines as no man's land?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you draw a line around Nedzarici from -- starting from - if it's appropriate - the forward positions of the Bosnian Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as we shall have to go back -- we shall have problems later on to find these lines, perhaps we should have that explained somehow, in some way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll do that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please place the initials or the initial P alongside the line indicating the forward position of the Presidency forces?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now place the letter S alongside the forward positions for the Bosnian Serb forces. Before you do that -- all right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now place an N alongside the line indicating the boundary of Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the -- that line runs from one yellow road to another. Do the yellow roads mark the remaining boundaries of Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Nedzarici was never bounded by the two yellow lines or the two yellow roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm pointing -- I had in mind the yellow roads further to the west and north, the airport road, I think it is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, west and north, yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were they the other boundaries --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Remember the pause. Could you take your pen and indicate that section of road which completes the boundaries of Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, yesterday, you told us that you have some video footage of the Bosnian Serb -- or the barracks in Nedzarici. Would you please outline those barracks? You have taken off the first map and put on it another map.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Firstly, what is the map you have now placed on the ELMO? Where did that map come from?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map was provided by General Zivanovic who was the very first Serb commander who I dealt with in terms of the airport agreement, opening the airport and the first agreement for the concentration of weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, are you able to indicate the position of the barracks on the first map?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't, because it's not on it. It's off the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say it's --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's off the map, it's down here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just wait for a minute, if you would. Are you consulting this map in order to find the barracks in Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I asked you if you could locate the barracks in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedzarici, I can find those, yeah, no problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well put the --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, we'll put the other one back. I'm sorry. I thought you were talking about the barracks in Lukavica. Okay. The barracks in Nedzarici are down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take the blue pen and draw on the map the outline of the barracks for Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I could just clarify something you said yesterday, on the video, you told us there was some footage of the barracks at Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as of -- I withdraw that. Did you know a building --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could Mr. Ierace, could the witness put a B next to where he indicated the barracks were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Inside the symbol, thank you. Now, do you know of a building in Nedzarici known as the school of theology?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you place --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was used as a hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you place a cross indicating the position and alongside the cross, capital letter T.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you visit that building complex?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was and if you don't --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that? You said you remember and now you are reaching for a document in your briefcase. Before you look at the document, can you tell us if you remember or not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do remember it but I just need to actually refer to the date. We're talking about something that happened 11 years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same night that the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please wait. And you told us you did remember. Can you please wait, sir, and not look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object. The witness was about to explain why he was remembering and how he was remembering, he was saying "the same night as" and he was interrupted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but at the same time, the witness tried to -- Mr. Gray, may I ask you -- sometimes you will first be asked whether you remember something and sometimes if you have no clear recollection on details there might be other sources to refresh your recollection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- And certainly if you say, "I remembered that it was a certain day when this or that happened, but I do not know the exact date," please tell us and in the next questions, further clarification will be sought by the parties. So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I ask to actually refer to my documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact that you will first be asked whether you still know it and no one will be surprised after 11 years that you would not know specific dates, and then if it's of importance to know even if it's not in your recollection but you have sources available, that would allow you to reconstruct what date it was, you'll certainly be asked by the parties and then, having asked to do so, you may consult whatever you'd like to consult as long as you indicate what you are consulting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that you don't remember the date that you could refresh your memory from the document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of document is it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my witness --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Statement that I gave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do. And could you tell us on what page of the statement that appears?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will do when I find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you are looking for a reference to Nedzarici, could I direct you to page 6, the entry for the 18th of May. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not it. That's not it. It's later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To save time, would you mind looking at that during the first break and --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fine, no problem, but I know it's in here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you about it when we return.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, no problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that it was used as a hospital, by whom?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the Serbs had a temporary -- it was like a -- in military terms we would call it a regimental aid post, okay? It was an RAP. They could only do very primary things on that and in order to get their casualties who were more seriously wounded they had to take them from there through machine-gun alley, from Nedzarici to Ilidza where Ilidza had a better medical facility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right and did they use an APC for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't have any in Nedzarici. They didn't have any armoured vehicles. There were no armoured vehicles in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What weaponry did you see in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Small arms and that's all. Small arms and that is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No mortars?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No tanks?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No APCs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you visit Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there at least three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an observation post, a UN observation post in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I was trying to arrange one and that was part of the -- what I call the second agreement to actually concentrate all weapons and that's why they actually redecorated, I mean repainted and redecorated and showed me the kitchen and whatever for the observers to actually occupy the quarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts was the observation post to be if it was set up? Which quarters?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was going to be in the barracks at the highest point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were living in Nedzarici, let's say, by September, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no real idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it there were a number of Bosnian Serb troops?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Combatants?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any civilians in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the map, and accepting, for the moment, that the blue grids are a kilometre square, would it be fair to say that Nedzarici was less than one kilometre at its widest point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be very close to one kilometre. I think it would be slightly wider. I mean in terms of east to west, it would probably be only probably a kilometre but from north to south it would probably be 1.5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that Nedzarici was strategically important from the perspective of the Bosnian Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that it received quite a pounding by Presidency forces. How was it if they only had small arms, did not even have mortars, let alone any form of armoured vehicles that they could resist such force?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can I ask you, did you review the videotapes and did you see the tanks which were knocked out on the way to the airport? Did you see those tanks?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's -- in general terms, Mr. Gray, you're first required to answer the question and if you'd like to make reference to a video you're aware of that exists, you can do so. And I think you may assume that the parties have, as good as they could, viewed the videos you presented.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm very sorry. The pounding that happened in Nedzarici happened basically from Stup, from 122, I mean I was there and I told you that yesterday, they were from 122 Howitzers from the Croats. Okay. They came very clearly from -- and I can indicate on the map, Stup is here, we have Nedzarici here, okay. The Croat commander, okay, I can -- I can even show you probably the house that he actually lived in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please wait a minute. Regardless of where that particular pounding came from --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness answered and gave precise indications, I think for the transcript it would be important to indicate clearly what he has pointed to on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think we know Mr. Stup is and I think we know where Nedzarici is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the witness pointed to where on the map it's indicated Stup and in general terms if we are talking about specific places, buildings, et cetera, this should certainly be indicated on the map or precisely described. If in more general terms we are referring for example to bring -- then it's not under all circumstances necessary to point out where exactly it was. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regardless of who carried out that particular barrage of shelling, would not the Presidency forces have capitalised on the effects of that barrage and moved in on Nedzarici if there was no significant resistance left, they would not stand idly by, would they?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No they tried to and they lost a lot of casualties and it's very important that -- I mean I spoke to the Serbian commander who was in command of Nedzarici and they found amongst the bodies of the Muslims forces that were killed in that attack, they found people with -- I'm sorry, dark skin, and dark-skinned people don't live in the former Yugoslavia. They don't live there. They were mercenaries or they were volunteers, they were from a different country and they were found in no man's land and I can show you exactly where --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop for a minute. Please stop. Why do you mention that? Why in response to the question I asked you and I invite you to read that question on the screen, do you offer to this Trial Chamber that amongst the bodies of the Muslims, quoting your words, Muslim forces, they found people with dark skin? Why is that so important for you to mention? What are you trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to tell you that the Presidency forces had reinforcements from other countries and that they were not Yugoslavs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you reread the question I asked you? If not, please do.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, perhaps before the witness answers, I want to object. I think it would be good, according to the custom, that Mr. Ierace checks first what the knowledge and information of the witness is and to find out whether what he can offer about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... If you would object to that question, then you should have done it at that time and not after the answer given and after the next question of Mr. Ierace. Mr. Ierace is now moving to, at least is putting new questions to the witness in respect of the answer the witness has given and it's now not the moment to object. And apart from that, Mr. Ierace only asked the question to read the question. I didn't hear him say that he would like to have again an answer on the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That answer has nothing to do with the question I asked you, does it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, you can read it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will read the question again. I will put the question to you, Mr. Gray. The question was and it might not be on your screen anymore, but -- the question was: "Regardless of who carried out that particular barrage of shelling, would not the Presidency forces have capitalised on the effects of that barrage and moved in on the territory if there was no significant resistance left, they would not stand idly by, would they?" And after having repeated this question as put to you by Mr. Ierace, the question you are asked to answer is whether your mentioning of people from outside the former Yugoslavia and that was part of your answer relates in any way to what you were asked about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not a matter of apologising. It's just Mr. Ierace seeks your answer to the question whether you answered related to what he asked you so --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the Muslims would have, if they could have, but on the videotape that you have, the Court has, you can quite clearly see two tanks, you can see a lot of tank rounds, you can see the effort that the Presidency side put in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, Mr. Gray, you are now answering the question that I read to you, but the next question to you was whether the answer you initially gave to that question in which you mentioned that people with the black -- dark skin were found, whether that answer that you gave relates in whatever way with the question put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does relate to the question put to me because the Presidency forces used what I would call irregular or mercenary forces in order to try and take Nedzarici. They were killed, they were found on the field of battle, they were recovered, they were buried from the field of battle and if the Presidency force could have taken Nedzarici, then they would have, but they didn't have sufficient forces to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We'll come back to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the meantime, will you please take out your statement and turn to page 6.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The third paragraph, does that commence with the date 18 May?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll read it out, please follow it and check that I am reading it correctly. "18 May was a busy day. The generator house at the Rainbow hotel took a direct hit. The Bosnians had snipers in the newspaper building next to the Rainbow hotel shooting at the Serbs. The Serbs return fire was hitting the rainbow hotel. I met the men who had been shelling the apartment building where I was living. He was the deputy commander of the Serbs in Nedzarici. He came out with one of his lieutenants and spoke to me outside the Rainbow hotel."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please read not too quickly, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. "He admitted firing mortars at the apartments I lived in because that was now the front line. He spoke excellent English."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I correctly read that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign the statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was what I read out at the time you signed the statement the truth?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you forgotten about the mortars?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not forgotten about the mortars and I have not forgotten about the fire that was coming from the apartment buildings that I was living in, that was going towards the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you not think it is contradictory on the one hand to say that the Bosnian Serb forces in Nedzarici had no mortars and on the other hand, to say that on the 18th of May, 1992, their deputy commander admitted to you that he was responsible for firing mortar shells at the place where you lived?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you may have a point, but I think that the mortar shells more probably came from Ilidza which is just a very small distance away from Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please stop for a minute. Are you now telling us that you think he lied when he said to you that he had fired the mortars or are you saying that he directed mortar fire from a mortar battery at Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been either position because they were both in range of where the apartment buildings were. They were both in range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, General Galic, you are standing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President, I would like to confer with my lawyers, please, now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then stop for a while and give an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask for another 30 seconds of patience? Thank you very much. Mr. President, I have a belated objection. It is belated but I'm going to be very clear. Mr. Ierace's question was as follows and exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wonder whether this should be in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this something --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness can hear this. He can hear this because it has to do with the question that was asked by Mr. Ierace and I seem to have already -- Mr. Ierace's question was: Did you see Nedzarici and so on and so forth. "See," it is very precise. He is being asked very precisely, did you see the mortars and then he talks and then he is trapped because he says something else he says that he never saw those mortars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That should not have been discussed in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly then I will speak later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I ask you whether it was something you said it was no problem you were discussing the whole matter in the presence of the witness which is not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, my apologies. Very well. May I continue in the absence of the witness? May I continue in the absence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll ask the witness to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. President, I believe to have said that a few hours ago or perhaps yesterday that one needed to respect certain rules. The question on page 17, line -- also 17 so it's 17, 17 was as follows: [In English] [Previous translation continues]... In Nedzarici [Interpretation] And after that about mortars and the witness answered no and he said that he had been to Nedzarici only three times and then a trap is being set because a commander tells him that he admitted to him that he had fired but in his written statement he doesn't say that he saw these mortars and then he refers to a contradiction which doesn't really exist and he raises this with the witness when the witness said very clearly one is attempting to interpret it in the sense which is opposite to what the witness said. So this is my objection and I really find that this manner of work absolutely does not agree, is completely at variance with accepted rules. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I noticed that the witness, as far as I understand his answers, did not make that distinction. Where he said, "you've got a point and I think they might have been fired from somewhere else" and the problem is that the witness started saying that they did not have certain things and then the next question was: What did you see? Yes. We'll clarify the issue. The witness may be brought in again. It was not appropriate to deal with it in the presence of the witness, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. On the other hand, I do agree with you that the contradiction as put by Mr. Ierace to the witness was not as firm as it perhaps at first sight looked like. I'll try to clarify the issue and we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I respond to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I should have given you an opportunity to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, while the contradiction put to the witness is not as firm as it at perhaps first sight might look, the witness in his explanation allowed for another possibility and that was acknowledged by me in the follow-up question. So my point is where is the confusion, where is the misunderstanding on the part of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I made already an observation on that. I said that from the answers of the witness, he -- it seems that there was no confusion. I'll ask the usher to bring the witness into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, may I ask you for some clarification? You told us earlier this afternoon that the Serb -- that in Nedzarici, that they had not have any armoured vehicles. There were no armoured vehicles in Nedzarici. You are then subsequently asked what weaponry did you see in Nedzarici and you said: "Small arms and that's all." Small arms and that's all. You were then asked, "no mortars?" Your answer was no. You were then asked, "no tanks?" Your answer was no. And then you were asked, "no APCs?" And your answer was no. By saying no, did you intend to say that you just didn't see mortars or tanks or APCs in Nedzarici or that they were not there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, that is exactly what I am saying. I am saying that I physically did not see them in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They might have been there --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They may have been there but I physically did not see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, does that apply to APCs as well that they could have been in Nedzarici but you did not see them?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could have been there but I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the last time that you visited Nedzarici approximately?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I need to refer to my notes to actually --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come back to that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to find that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commander admitted to you, that is, the deputy commander of the Serbs in Nedzarici that he was shelling your apartment building and his explanation was that he did so because that was now the front line?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else lived in the Rainbow hotel at that stage?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that stage there were still UN people living in the Rainbow hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What further explanation, if any, did he give as to why he was mortaring the Rainbow hotel, apart from the fact that he regarded it as the front line?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no explanation given. None.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you think that it was legitimate for him to shell the Rainbow hotel at that stage?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the difference in range between the apartments where I was living and the actual Rainbow hotel, you'll find that the difference is very -- it's only about 200 metres. And the -- mortars are not precise weapons, they are an area weapon. They will not land within -- unless you fire them from a very short range, they are not a precise weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Who else lived in the apartment block where you lived, if anyone?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you the names of my neighbours, if you like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. Approximately how many people were there living in that building at that stage?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were hundreds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you think it appropriate that your apartment building should have been shelled at that stage, and by appropriate, I mean legitimate?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has -- the objection has to do with the answer that was given to the previous question by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You previously answered a question by saying that a mortar was an imprecise weapon, did you mean to say at that time that you considered the shell or shells hitting the place where you were living as a result of imprecise targeting, that it was not your building that was being targeted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the building was definitely targeted because there was fire coming from the building, machine-gun fire coming from my building towards the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this building have hundreds of civilians living in it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did it also had -- and on the videotapes, you can see armoured personnel carriers from the Presidency forces moving around exactly next to my apartment building -- I mean, right outside my front door, you can see an armoured personnel carrier and the building was occupied not only with civilians but also with Presidency forces who were firing at the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many storeys did that being have?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eight, I think, eight or nine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how far was it from the front line position of the Serb forces? I withdraw that question. Could you point to the apartment building in question? That is the position on the map?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just going to show it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apartment building was here, there it is there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it front on to, that is did it front on to directly on to Ante Babicka Street that is the yellow road to left of the number three running in a north-south direction?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, given that there was fire from your building, placing yourself, for the moment, in the shoes of the deputy commander of the Bosnian Serb forces in Sarajevo, or at least considering his position, would you think it appropriate for him, that is, legitimate, to respond to snipers operating from an apartment building accommodating hundreds of people, to respond with mortars?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is highly speculative, Mr. President, because the witness is asked to speak through -- to assume somebody else's role.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, firstly, that was also highly inappropriate to express in front of the witness. Secondly, as it happens, the Defence chose to invite this witness to comment legitimacy of return fire yesterday no less and the witness was able to offer an opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That question which the Defence asked -- was always concerned with the fact that one should be governed by principles and we never wanted the question -- our questions to be as subjectivised. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Line 31, 7, is a question, not an answer. That's the question we are dealing with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I had some difficulties in catching it on the screen where it reads answer -- my recollection that it was your question, Mr. Ierace, am I correct when you said, "placing yourself at the moment in the shoes of the deputy commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note, I'm now rereading the question there are some words missing from the transcript. Perhaps I should rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question will be rephrased then. In general terms, I would say that although one could wonder whether it would always assist the Chamber highly to know the opinion of a witness about what was legitimate or not, sometimes we are interested to know what the view of the witness on that issue is. The Defence has asked that for many, many times so therefore as such, this such a question is not prohibited. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gray --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you would rephrase the question any how. Yes, that was just a comment in general subject matter, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that there was outgoing fire from the apartment building in which hundreds of people were living. The deputy commander of the Bosnian Serb forces in Nedzarici said he was responsible for that and his only explanation was that the apartment block where you lived was now part of the front line. Do you think that it was legitimate, lawful, if you like, for a commander in that position to use mortar fire to respond to machine-gun fire from an apartment complex with hundreds of people living there?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must ask and I apologise to the witness but I must ask him to go out. No, I'll phrase it differently but I'd rather not be reprimanded, Mr. President. No, no, I will phrase it differently. We do not know what formation did the -- this order have subjectively speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll put the question to the witness. When you were told that the apartment block was shelled, did you form any opinion as to whether, according to your knowledge and experience, long-standing knowledge and experience as a military man, whether this would be a legitimate target and with this weaponry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was appropriate from the point of view that the Muslims were actually not only sniping and firing from my apartment building, they were also using the apartment buildings and I saw this with my own eyes, they were actually using it to -- as a what we'd call a forming up place which is where you form your troops before you actually attack and I saw them physically with the headbands on, the different colours for all the different companies and platoons and so on, and they were using it and they were coming out from behind the apartment buildings and they were attacking Nedzarici. So yes, if I was in the shoes of the commander of Nedzarici, I would have used mortars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I understand your testimony to be that apart from what he told you, that you, yourself, had information that would, in your view, make it a legitimate target, irrespective of what he told you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of day did the mortar shells hit your apartment block?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them -- one of them hit and I think I've got recorded in the statement here that one of them hit about 5.00 in the morning. Others hit the building at about -- about the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On more than one day?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. During the break, can you find that reference to 5.00 in the morning in your statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can try to find it, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you regard a mortar as an appropriate weapon to use against a gunning placement, that is, a small arms type of gunning placement, inside an apartment block?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has already answered this question in his preceding answer -- I mean his previous answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the answer was not just about this question, the answer dealt with matters that were outside the question as well. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'll read it back to you. Would you regard a mortar as an appropriate weapon to use against a gunning placement, that is, a small arms type of gunning placement operating from inside an apartment block?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would. You use every force available to you. I mean what force you have available to you to actually counter the people -- I picked up dead bodies from Nedzarici, okay? People had been shot through the head. One of them had been in the national Yugoslav basketball team, he was so long we couldn't fit him in the APC we had to leave the back doors open. He was over 7 feet tall and I picked up those bodies from Nedzarici. They were shot through the head and when you have someone killed by sniper fire, you reply with the maximum force available. That is what war is all about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what regards, sir, do you have for civilians on the other side when you return fire, if any?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean we weren't returning any fire. I mean, the civilians basically moved from the very front wall of the apartment building, they moved into the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please stop for a minute. I think you've misunderstood my question. I'm not referring to return fire from the UN. I'm saying, in relation to that picture you paint, that position of the Bosnian Serb commander, what regard should he have for civilian casualties on the other side when he returns fire?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, I mean, that's purely subjective.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by that? Do you mean that's a matter for him?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean that they were taking civilian casualties as well and war is war is war. I mean you have to accept that there will be civilian casualties and what he was trying to do was to ward off the people who were firing, and I mean it's on the videotape, you can see it. He was trying to ward off the people who were firing at him and killing his people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could just stop you there for a minute. We understand that the position of many of the commanders of troops during this armed conflict had to respond to fire coming from urban areas. What I'm asking you to comment on is the appropriateness of the type of weapon that you used in that situation, a particular instance that you've told us about was an apartment block accommodating hundreds of people --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. Could the witness please leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gray, it would be time any how for a break so in order to prevent that you have to go out, return again, we'll have a break for some 20 minutes and we'll not bother you at this moment with your procedural issues. Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Gray out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Gray, I think you would still try to find the day in your statement, I think, when you visited the school of theology; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do that -- you were asked to look during the break whether you could find the date on which you visited the school of theology, so if you would use your time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in Nedzarici. If you would please do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, my objection is as follows: Mr. Ierace said this question and talks about the appropriateness of a shot at a building in which there are several hundreds of persons, not civilians. But the first thing he should have established and he did not establish - I mean Mr. Ierace - is the hypothetical knowledge whether he -- whether the Serb commander knew that there were also many Serb civilians in that building because on one hand, he -- because other witnesses have told us that they lived on the other side from this facade which was exposed to the fire so if the commander did not have the exact knowledge that the civilians were living there, then this question lacks proper ground so hence my action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first try to clarify the issue. I think the question was that -- of course the witness cannot answer whether another person would consider the target to be legitimate. To that extent there is some hypothetical aspect in the question any how but having clarified this as far as I understand the question, I'd like to give Mr. Ierace an opportunity to respond to the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my starting point is one of the two occasions yesterday that the Defence raised this issue, the Defence asked this question at 17.15 or thereabouts, having raised the issue of night-time attacks over the city of Sarajevo, "Thank you, Colonel. The Serbian reaction, was it normal, was it abnormal from a military point of view was it understandable?" Answer: "It was probably disproportionate to what was going out. What was coming in from the Serbs was certainly a lot heavier but they had a lot more weapons when one or two rounds out and ten rounds came in, it was just a fact of war. Question: "Very well."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you slow down, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will slow down. "If we put aside the issue of the proportionality of the response, was the response a legitimate one according to your professional experience or was it not a legitimate one? Answer: When you get fired at, you normally fire back so yes." Mr. President, that was the second time that the Defence raised this issue, called upon this witness as an expert, if you like, as an experienced commander, to comment on the legitimacy of actions he observed in Sarajevo. But when it is done now by the Prosecution, they interrupt regularly, frequently, I think now for the fourth time. Mr. President, you said earlier that it was of dubious assistance to the Trial Chamber. If it is not of assistance and if that is clearly understood then I won't pursue this issue, that is, this witness' opinions of legitimacy and of lawfulness any further, but if it is an open issue in terms of this witness, then I do respectfully seek the opportunity to press him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I said one could wonder whether it would always assist the Chamber. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, Mr. Ierace confronts you with what he considers to be similar questions put yesterday to you by the witness and his opinion that it would be inappropriate to object to questions similar to those you put yourself to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I will respond very briefly. In this particular case, the Prosecution didn't seek to get general answers. The Prosecution used very precise terms. They mentioned date and situation, date, situation and we have other expressions and I can find them. We have here, for instance, this is page 36, line 15, a particular instance, specific situation, and we have the apartment building accommodating hundreds of people. So here we are talking about a particular situation but the objection is the following: What did the commander know about this particular situation? Unless we know the facts, the question has no foundation. The question we asked was of a general nature. For instance if we are using a mortar -- mobile mortar, is it then legitimate to respond with counter-battery. I didn't say was it legitimate for this mortar to be used on this day and so on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is my recollection correct that on many specific incidents, witnesses have testified about that you asked whether and for what reasons this witness considered the place where, for example, a shell landed to be a legitimate target, very specific on very specific targets? That's my first question. My second question would be such a question put in general terms would be more admissible for what specific reason than if put in respect to a specific event?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, because if we are asking a question how something was done, then imply a fact that a commander under the orders of General Galic therefore and implying the responsibility of General Galic would have then attacked this apartment, fired on the target, that could be a civilian facility so this is one subjective aspect which is what I mentioned earlier. In any case, the answer of the witness was very interesting but this way of proceeding is very different from a general way, for instance, asking a question and saying, firing on an apartment block in which there are active soldiers preparing operations, is that a legitimate target? That is a neutral question and acceptable in the eyes of the Defence but the way the Prosecution asked the question, putting the -- yourself in the shoes of the commander now that is a different way of asking a question, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My last question: If you put a question on whether a certain place would be a legitimate target because there was soldiers there, in your line of reasoning, would it be relevant to know whether the one who ordered this target to be attacked would know about the presence of soldiers there just as you indicated that it was of importance to know for those who were in charge to know whether they were aware of civilians living there. It's not my recollection, but correct me if I am wrong that when questions were put to witnesses whether certain buildings or certain structures were legitimate targets, that I do not remember that you asked, as a previous question, whether the person who would fire at such an object would know about the presence of what you might consider it to make a legitimate target.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would appreciate a precise example on your part, but what can I say off the top of my head is that the question that was asked was as a general. How can we get to the HQ if it is located in the town and if we cannot have a direct access to it? This is a general question that was asked which would not imply a subjectivism and the questions in a general rule from posed in this way and I believe that, yours if I may be allowed, at asking a certain expert with what would you attack an HQ which was located in a lower part of the building. These are the question we're asking and we believe that we are asking them particularly if we are referring to a commander that we don't know who he is or what he did at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will give a decision after the break. We'll adjourn until 6.00. Yes, there's one issue I should deal with before the break. There would be a possibility to sit tomorrow morning instead of tomorrow in the afternoon. It would not create any extra time. Would there be any opposition from the parties to sit in the morning rather than the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For General Galic, I don't know but for his counsel, that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, General Galic, would there be any problem as far as you are concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no problems with that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we could live with that. I would prefer that we sat in the afternoon but we could comply with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then subject to checking the agendas of the bench and all those who have to be present, we'll then sit tomorrow in the morning in courtroom 2. Yes. We now adjourn until 6.00. --- Break taken at 5.40 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, you may escort the witness into the courtroom. The Chamber still owes you a decision, the objection is denied, at the same time, Mr. Ierace, spending too much time on the issue seems not to be very useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Understood, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will sit tomorrow in the morning, courtroom 2 from 9.00 until quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in the meantime, may I know why, although I can guess, why is the objection rejected? So for future reference?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied because the Chamber has accepted and -- similar questions whether of a general nature, whether in a specific part that what we learn from it is what a witness, at least we can guess, has been taught as to legitimacy of targets. The Chamber has also expressed that it's -- perhaps that one could wonder to what extent these questions could assist the Chamber because the Chamber is of the opinion that whether a target is legitimate or not depends on what the witness tells us about that but what the Chamber finds finally. So therefore it's a bit mixed at the one hand, the Chamber is not greatly assisted but to the extent it assists these questions are not inadmissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, Mr. Ierace will resume the cross-examination. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, when you spoke to the deputy commander, did you make clear to him that there was civilians living in the apartment block where you lived?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the apartment blocks remain a target to the Bosnian Serb forces after that day?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did mortars from time to time remain weapons used by the Bosnian Serb forces against targets within the apartment block?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, very infrequently. They were only -- the apartment blocks were only hit maybe three or four times, that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- I withdraw that. In relation to the position of UN forces, you have told us some of the history of the PTT. When did the UN first place personnel in the headquarters at Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd have to refer to my diary but it was in late June, early July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you regard the headquarters where UN personnel were placed as a legitimate military target for forces of the Bosnian Presidency?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were there to actually try and bring some peace. We were there to actually observe the concentration of weapons and we were -- we had very clear indications that -- I mean we had a UN flag flying outside, for instance, Lukavica barracks and the building that was next to the Presidency where we had our headquarters as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
